conclusion: The retained Triton vecadd descriptor preload is 12 DWORDs, covering 48 bytes, and remains incompatible with the current native mapping/entry semantics; both wire validation and local admission must fail closed rather than strip, zero, or reinterpret it.
decision: Carry descriptor_preload_dwords through MAP metadata, return NOT_SUPPORTED for the 12-DWORD artifact before publishing a mapping or admitting a packet, and keep launcher/JIT/execution/fallback false until preload-aware mapping plus entry semantics have dedicated evidence.
invalidated_assumptions: A local owner-bound mapper may ignore preload because no GPU execution is claimed yet.
The value 12 can be treated as 12 bytes or silently replaced with zero while retaining the same Triton code-object identity.
Passing MAP/ALLOC/SUBMIT lifecycle tests for a zero-preload fixture makes the retained Triton vecadd launchable.
observation: The pinned 5,408-byte Triton HSACO still encodes descriptor preload 12 DWORD (48 bytes); CP23 protocol and native-state paths report it unsupported before publication/admission, while compiler_invoked, JIT, launcher, GPU execution, and fallback remain false.
question_or_symptom: Why must CP23 reject the retained Triton vecadd image even though its generic wire fields and 48-byte kernarg range are otherwise representable?
